contributions.statement: Anchor code-graph context on the agent's own lexical hits: expand each grep match to confidence-filtered structural neighbors (imports, callers/callees, type hierarchy, linked tests) instead of graph-first retrieval; this lifted file-level Acc@5 by +11.8 points with fixed hyperparameters over the strongest baseline, and graph expansion was the largest ablation contributor.
contributions.evidence: §5.2 Table 1 (LocBench), §5.3 Table 3 (component ablation on MuLocBench). Python-only localization; MuLocBench and downstream SWE-Atlas gains over Claude Code are ~1 point without variance; nothing released.

contributions.statement: Deliver graph evidence inside existing search-tool output rather than adding separate graph tools to the agent's catalog.
contributions.evidence: §5.2 comparison against separate-graph-tool agents (LocAgent, CoSIL); this is a cross-system comparison, not a controlled ablation of delivery mode.
relative_to: 2607.19653 injected deterministic tool output beats asking the agent to call the tool

reason: The lexical-anchoring condition plus a clean graph-expansion ablation adds to the KB's code-graph evidence; the 'inline beats separate tool' claim is suggestive only. For Java the graph would come from an LSP or compiler index.
